Years ago, MacBook came with a slot that allowed you to secure the computer to a table leg or similar fixture with a cable lock. It was a lifesaver when you wanted to leave your laptop at a table in a coffee shop while you went up to the counter to order another drink, without having to carry it around with you.

That slot has long since disappeared, but adapters are now available that let you lock down your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro…

If you remember the anti-theft slots on either side of the chassis, you’ve probably been using a MacBook for quite some time. Those slots were designed for T-shaped accessories that you insert into the slot and then turn 90 degrees to lock in place. The most common design was a cable loop that could be passed through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock is now repackaging that idea with an adapter that fits on the corner of a MacBook, allowing you to lock the machine down with a cable lock. The adapter is a two-piece design that clamps onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has added a MacBook Neo version alongside the original MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It should be emphasised that these locks have always been extremely low-security devices, designed only to stop someone from casually swiping your MacBook during the few seconds when you’re not paying attention. I’m happy to use one myself in small coffee shops where I can still see my table when I go up to the counter for a refill, but I would never rely on a lock to keep an eye on my machine if it’s out of my line of sight.

At $70 each, the adapter isn’t cheap, especially since you also have to buy the lock itself separately; but if you have a lock gathering dust in a drawer somewhere, you might decide it’s worth bringing back into service.
